subsystems.name: Sensing layer
subsystems.role: measures what the city is doing, continuously.

subsystems.name: Connectivity and edge compute
subsystems.role: moves and pre-processes data without sending everything to a central server.

subsystems.name: Digital twin
subsystems.role: a live 3D model of buildings, roads, pipes and networks that mirrors current conditions.

subsystems.name: Coordination engine
subsystems.role: turns the twin's predictions into schedules and set-points.

subsystems.name: Participation layer
subsystems.role: lets residents set goals, deliberate and challenge automated decisions.

buildSteps.title: Instrument the city
buildSteps.detail: Deploy sensors and meters district by district, with published rules on what is collected and what is never collected.

buildSteps.title: Build a shared data layer
buildSteps.detail: Agree common formats and APIs so transport, energy and water systems feed one stream instead of separate silos.

buildSteps.title: Construct the digital twin
buildSteps.detail: Combine survey, satellite and building data into a 3D model, then connect it to the live stream so it updates in near real time.

buildSteps.title: Add simulation
buildSteps.detail: Run traffic, flood, heat and energy models against the twin to predict what a change would do before it is made.

buildSteps.title: Build the coordination engine
buildSteps.detail: Optimise signals, transit and demand response against agreed objectives — noting this is mathematical optimisation plus machine learning, not a 'consensus AI'.

buildSteps.title: Build the participation layer
buildSteps.detail: Give residents a way to set priorities, deliberate and vote, with results recorded openly.

buildSteps.title: Link decisions to actuation
buildSteps.detail: Connect approved strategies to real controllers, with rate limits, fail-safes and the ability to revert instantly.

buildSteps.title: Audit and iterate
buildSteps.detail: Publish outcomes, test for bias and error, and let the public and independent auditors inspect the rules.

prerequisites.tech: Cheap dense IoT sensing and connectivity
prerequisites.why: continuous city-wide measurement is the input the whole idea depends on.
real projects exist — Singapore's Virtual Singapore is one — but most cover a single domain or a district, not a whole city live.
without shared formats, transport, energy and water data never combine into one picture.
no deployed system can explain and justify city-wide trade-offs to the satisfaction of an electorate.
fine-grained sensing conflicts with surveillance unless aggregation and retention rules are enforced.
tools such as Pol.is in Taiwan's vTaiwan process and participatory budgeting, which began in Porto Alegre in 1989, work in defined settings but not as continuous city governance.

pathway.milestone: single-domain digital twins and optimisers: adaptive traffic signals, grid demand response, district energy
pathway.unlocks: measurable savings and trust in the data layer.

pathway.milestone: multi-domain city twins that link transport, energy and water, with published performance data
pathway.unlocks: trade-offs across systems rather than within one.

pathway.milestone: institutional participation platforms with binding, auditable input on priorities
pathway.unlocks: legitimacy for automated decisions, and a route to accountability when they are wrong.

pathway.milestone: continuous, city-wide coordination with human oversight and hard limits on automation
pathway.unlocks: the stated goal — but only if privacy, fairness and reversibility are solved first. The literal 'hive-mind' version, where a shared AI settles city affairs by consensus, remains speculation.
